missing: Efficacy, cart19-nsg-xenograft track: NCT01747486 CTL019 randomized dose-optimization in R/R CLL, primary 'Number of Patients Achieving Complete Response Within 3 Months', results posted 2019-02-26 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01747486); Frey 2020 JCO doi:10.1200/JCO.19.03237 reports CR 28% (90% CI 16-44%) at 4 weeks. Earliest scored efficacy entry (likely same, partial), dated 2019, not 2023.

Safety, cll-ibrutinib-cart19-xenograft track: Gauthier 2020 (doi:10.1182/blood.2019002936) cites preclinical data that ibrutinib reduces CRS (Ruella et al., Clin Cancer Res 2017, xenograft; DOI not verified here) and reports lower CRS severity and cytokines with concurrent ibrutinib: a stated safety comparison (likely same) with no entry.

Antibody arm, inebilizumab: MEDI-551 B-cell depletion in human-CD19 transgenic mice (Herbst et al., JPET 2010; not verified this session) and its cynomolgus toxicology (BLA 761142 pharm/tox, not in bundle) have no engagement/dose/safety track; inebilizumab B-cell depletion in CLL/NMOSD patients would be the comparison.
rule_questions: Is a model of a combination regimen (CD19 CAR-T plus ibrutinib, a non-member BTK inhibitor) in scope for the CD19-depleter class, or does it fall under 'a member drug outside the class'? It decides whether the cll-ibrutinib-cart19-xenograft track exists at all.
When an incremental prediction (drug X improves class member Y) is followed only by a single-arm combination trial meeting its primary endpoint, is that same (direction) or untested (no comparator)?
Dose margin_stated: monkey NOAEL existed before FIH but was public only in the 2020 FDA review; does an unpublished pre-trial margin count as 'stated before the trial'?
For engagement, does clinical response/lymphocyte clearance count as a PD readout for an ex-vivo cytotoxicity model, and at which readout_tier?

Dose/safety retrodiction: is regulator-filed toxicology run before first-in-human (model_filed: true) but first public later a retrodiction? The 2026-11-09 ruling says yes; the brief's 'public earlier' wording does not say against what.

Efficacy retrodiction for a combination or comparative model (CAR-T + ibrutinib xenograft; MEDI-551 vs rituximab ADCC): does an earlier same-target monotherapy patient result make the model a retrodiction when the patients had not yet tested the combination or the comparison?
